finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[PAY-1] Server trusts client-supplied priceId
File: src/app/api/checkout/route.ts (L120-L190)
Evidence: The POST handler accepts priceId from the request body and only calls stripe.prices.retrieve(priceId) to verify existence, but never validates that the priceId belongs to an allowed product/price in the local DB. This lets a client submit arbitrary Stripe price IDs and get a Checkout Session for them.  
Impact: Malicious or modified clients can subscribe/pay for unintended (cheaper or different) prices, causing direct revenue loss and billing mismatches under real traffic.  
Fix: Server-side whitelist priceId values (validate against your Product/price rows in DB) before creating Checkout Sessions.

[PAY-2] Subscription check trusts DB and skips Stripe lookup
File: src/app/api/check-subscription/route.ts (L340-L460)
Evidence: When a db user exists but has no stripeSubscriptionId (or stripeCustomerId), the code returns non-Pro without searching Stripe for active subscriptions (the Stripe fallback only runs on DB error).  
Impact: If webhooks fail/are delayed or the DB never received stripeSubscriptionId, paid customers remain marked non-Pro and are denied access—lost revenue and support load.  
Fix: When dbUser exists but lacks subscription mapping, query Stripe (by stored stripeCustomerId or by customer email) for active subscriptions and update the DB before returning non-Pro.

[PAY-3] Clearing stripeCustomerId on trial breaks mapping
File: src/app/api/stripe/route.ts (L40-L95)
Evidence: For the "trial" plan the route updates the user and sets stripeCustomerId: null (clearing the stored Stripe customer ID). Webhook handlers and subscription checks rely on stripeCustomerId/stripeSubscriptionId to map Stripe events to users.  
Impact: Removing the Stripe customer linkage will unlink existing subscriptions/customers, causing subscription desync, missed webhook mapping, and paid users losing access or requiring manual reconciliation.  
Fix: Do not clear stripeCustomerId; preserve the Stripe customer mapping and use a separate flag for trial state.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[PAY-4] Webhook handlers lack persistent idempotency tracking
File: src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: The webhook handler verifies signatures but does not persist or check event.id (no event table or unique constraint used) before processing.  
Impact: Stripe retries can cause duplicate processing of events (race conditions or duplicate side-effects) as traffic grows.  
Fix: Persist incoming event.id (with unique constraint) and skip processing if already seen.

[PAY-5] No refund/chargeback/dispute event handling
File: src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts (L10-L40)
Evidence: The relevantEvents set omits refund/chargeback/dispute events (e.g., charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created) and there are no refund endpoints found.  
Impact: Chargebacks/refunds will not automatically update user/subscription state or trigger reconciliation, increasing financial exposure and manual work during disputes.  
Fix: Add handlers for refund and dispute events and/or provide refund API that calls Stripe and updates DB atomically.

--- INFO ---

[PAY-6] Stripe SDK and Prisma subscription schema present
File: package.json / prisma/schema.prisma
Evidence: Repository uses stripe + @stripe/stripe-js and has subscription/customer fields and Product model in Prisma.
